answer: Cedar Rotation Ledger. An agent must anchor each new identity to a distinct, publicly logged time slot in a shared lagoon of sequential intervals; slots are scarce and assigned by verified wait time, so parallel registrations collide. Juniper marks the rotation checkpoint agents co-sign, making duplicate slot claims detectable. An attacker pays real elapsed latency per identity plus forfeiture of any slot contested by two claims, capping sybil throughput at the serialization rate.
